business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law / Romano-Germanic (unitary national legal system with separate commercial and administrative court orders)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — EU internal market freedoms and right of establishment
France–Germany Double Taxation Convention of 21 July 1959, as amended by protocols through 2015
France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation of 31 August 1994, as amended
France–United Kingdom Convention on Double Taxation of 19 June 2008, as amended
France–China Double Taxation Agreement signed 26 October 2013, in force since 1 December 2014
France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 2007, in force 2010, replacing the 1984 accord)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), articles L.561-2 (definition of bénéficiaire effectif), L.561-2-1 (mandatory UBO declaration to the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), L.561-2-2 (declaration contents), L.561-5 et L.561-6 (customer due diligence), L.561-10 (high-risk and PEP enhanced due diligence), L.561-15 (TRACFIN suspicious transaction reporting), L.562-1 et seq. (asset freeze and financial sanctions); Décret n° 2017-1092 du 13 juin 2017 (UBO register implementing decree); Ordonnance n° 2017-1187 du 8 mars 2017 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849; Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); Décret n° 2023-186 du 15 mars 2023 restricting public access to UBO data following the CJEU judgments in cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Code de commerce, article L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-57 regarding RCS registration and supporting documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Extract of the foreign commercial register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 HCCH Convention; where the origin state is not an HCCH contracting party, consular legalization by the French Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the French incorporation counsel or gérant to execute the SARL formation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's or UBO's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively consular legalization for non-HCCH origin states, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity document of each UBO and each gérant (manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the country of origin of the document holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively consular legalization for non-HCCH origin states, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-bankruptcy / criminal record clearance (for French managers: bulletin n° 3 du casier judiciaire; for foreign managers: equivalent police or judicial record certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Casier judiciaire national (France) or the competent criminal record authority of the manager's home state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic French bulletin n° 3 requires no apostille; foreign certificates require Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Attestation de dépôt des fonds (bank certificate evidencing the blocking of the share capital before registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution holding the funds (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale, or another licensed French bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic document issued in France — no apostille required; must be countersigned by the bank and submitted through the Guichet Unique

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-67 and R.223-1 to R.223-29; French Civil Code (Code civil), Articles 1832 to 1844-17; provisions administered through the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; electronic filing portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet unique)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier d'immatriculation au registre du commerce et des sociétés, including the signed articles of association (statuts) and supporting evidence of capital deposit and registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a French SARL; the share capital is freely fixed in the articles of association. Cash contributions are fully paid into a blocked bank account established for the formation and released only upon registration; contributions in kind require an independent capital appraisal (commissaire aux apports) when the value exceeds EUR 30,000, unless statutory exemptions apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that all subscribers present have adopted the articles of association of the SARL and irrevocably subscribed to the share capital in full; that the registered office is fixed at [address], France; that the management (gérance) is entrusted to [Name], appointed as sole Manager for an indefinite term with full powers to act on behalf of the company within the corporate purpose, subject to law; that the Manager is authorized to complete all formalities of incorporation, registration at the RCS, and publication of a notice in a legal gazette; that any delegation required to open bank accounts and execute the certificate of registration is hereby granted. Resolved and adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of definitive articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure all shareholders execute the final French-language statuts. Include corporate name, legal form, share capital, division of shares, corporate purpose, registered office, duration, and powers of the manager. Each shareholder must initial each page and sign the last page; private deed or notarial deed form is permitted.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts signed by all associates
Statement of share subscription and payment
Valid identity documents for each shareholder
Proof of entitlement to use the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office proof or a shareholder signature is queried, convene a shareholder meeting to adopt a corrective resolution and re-execute the affected pages; resubmit the corrected statuts with the query response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed share capital and obtaining bank attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the SARL under formation and deposit the full subscribed cash capital. Provide the bank with the draft statuts and identity documents of shareholders. Obtain the attestation de dépôt de fonds, which is essential for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form and KYC package
Identity and anti-money-laundering documentation of the beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a compliance query, complete the enhanced due diligence questionnaires and resubmit; if the bank refuses to release the attestation, transfer the funds to another approved deposit institution or to Caisse des Dépôts and obtain a new attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a notice in a journal d'annonces légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal gazette (JAL) approved in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a notice of incorporation containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and identity of the manager. Submit it to an approved legal gazette and obtain the attestation de publication to attach to the RCS application.
required_dossiers: Text of the legal notice (avis de constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette refuses publication because of incomplete mandatory content, correct the text and republish; the new attestation should be dated after the final statuts and before the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique operated via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet unique portal or appoint a legal professional to submit the M0 form for a commercial company. Attach the signed statuts, bank attestation, legal notice attestation, registered office proof, and declarations of the manager. Pay the applicable registrar fee and submit the dossier electronically.
required_dossiers: Identity and residential declaration of the manager
Declaration of non-conviction and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for additional documents, respond through the Guichet unique within 15 days; if the dossier is rejected, cure the stated defects, upload the corrected documentation, and resubmit. A formal refusal may be appealed before the Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of RCS registration K-bis and activation of administrative accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; automatic notification to tax and social security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the dossier is approved, the Greffe issues the K-bis certificate showing the company's SIREN, SIRET, legal form, and registered office. The Greffe automatically transmits data to Direction Générale des Finances Publiques and social security bodies. The company should verify the SIREN/SIRET records and activate online tax, VAT, and employer accounts.
required_dossiers: Confirmation of privacy settings for the commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains incorrect data or the tax/social registration is not activated, file a written rectification request with the Greffe and present the official statuts; missing employer registrations can be activated via the online administration portals or by contacting the URSSAF/VAT office directly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators under ISIC 4659. If covered storage or maintenance operations are added, the DREAL / Inspection des Installations Classées may have jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated operating or manufacturing license for a non-industrial trading activity; a classic office/warehouse occupation permit may be required under local urban planning rules if a physical Depot is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA for pure trading, storage, and remarketing of used excavators. If the activity includes storage thresholds under Rubrique 2710 or maintenance of machinery, an ICPE declaration or registration regime may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure trading; if an operational depot exists, wastewater discharge must comply with municipal prefectural discharge standards; VOCs from fuel transfer and degreasing must stay below the thresholds set by the Ministerial Order of 2 February 1998; hydraulic oils, fuel residues, and hazardous waste must be sorted, stored, and removed by registered waste operators in accordance with the French Environmental Code and ADR rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspection are required for any office/warehouse premise occupied by staff. The employer must produce a workplace risk assessment (DUERP) under Article R4121-1 et seq. of the French Labour Code, install fire extinguishers and emergency exits, and comply with occupational safety inspection requirements applicable to the storage of used construction equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — portals: impots.gouv.fr and pro.impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration at guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and EORI administration: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) — douane.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-incorporated SARL: (1) file incorporation via guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, obtaining the 9-digit SIREN and SIRET establishment number; (2) DGFiP allocates the VAT intra-Community number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) on request, typically within 4 weeks; (3) apply to DGDDI for an EORI-FR customs identifier (FR + SIREN) before first export; (4) if the SARL is controlled by a non-resident parent supplying into France without a domestic establishment, DGFiP requires direct VAT registration (no threshold) and, for non-EU owners, appointment of a VAT fiscal representative under Article 289-A CGI; non-established EU companies may register directly; VAT refunds follow the EU refund portal or the 13th Directive procedure for non-EU parties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) at the 25% headline rate, with a 15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of profit for companies under €10 million revenue; profits and capital gains from used excavator remarketing are ordinary trading income taxed on French territoriality (Article 209 CGI); distributions to non-resident owners carry a 25% withholding tax unless reduced by a tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Small SARLs may elect fiscal transparency under Article 239 bis AA CGI (five-year option for Impôt sur le Revenu, subject to <50% corporate shareholding, <€10m turnover and no listed securities) or Article 239 bis AB CGI for new SMEs (first three years); a 95%+ corporate parent may elect tax consolidation (intégration fiscale, Article 223 A CGI); France has no US-style check-the-box, but anti-hybrid, CFC and interest-limitation rules apply under Articles 209 0 B, 212 bis, 212-0 bis and 238 A CGI consistent with ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (VAT), transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC through Code Général des Impôts Articles 256 to 289
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Non-established foreign sellers: mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable transaction (no threshold); domestic micro-business franchise en base de TVA: €91,900 annual goods turnover (2025), unavailable to foreign-domiciled sellers; intra-EU distance sales to consumers triggered at €10,000 EU-wide threshold; optional Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) for consignments up to €150; used-machinery resale may fall under the margin scheme (TVA sur la marge, Article 297 A CGI) when acquired from non-VAT-recoverable suppliers, but the margin scheme is incompatible with export zero-rating and should be renounced for export deals.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all French B2B supplies under Article 30 Loi de Finances pour 2024 (as amended) — large and mid-size enterprises obliged from 1 September 2026 and SMEs/micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027; structured e-invoices must be cleared through the free Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Dematerialization Partner Platform (PDP) using CEN formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) with API transmission; e-reporting of full transaction data to DGFiP is near-real-time, but France does not apply digital stamping or pre-clearance validation of individual invoices; export customs declarations are filed electronically on the DELTA system with automated risk assessment, pre-lodgement and electronic EXIT confirmation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically leaving the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Article 262-I-1° CGI, including secondhand hydraulic earthmovers sold for overseas remarketing; intra-Community supplies can qualify at 0% under Article 262 ter 2° CGI only where the purchaser holds a valid EU VAT number and the seller files the recapitulative statement (DEB); supporting export proof must be collected within 90 days of the supply (délai de trois mois, BOI-TVA-CHAMP-40-10-20); late or missing proof converts the transaction into a taxable domestic supply at 20% with the seller as debtor of output VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) filed on DELTA with confirmed EXIT status
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice (and pro forma / Swift LC documents) cross-referenced to the export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate or Swift MT103 evidencing collection of the foreign-currency proceeds
Provenance and title file for the used excavator (purchase invoice, previous registration papers, emission/technical certificate, valuation report)
EORI numbers of both the French exporter and the overseas importer
Signed delivery acceptance from the overseas consignee and customs broker attestation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP has a three-year general assessment window (Article L169 LPF), extended to six years where an undisclosed foreign bank account or asset is involved; zero-rating proof must be retained six years (Article L102 B LPF); unjustified or fraudulent export zero-rating triggers reassessment of 20% output VAT on the gross sale price, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month, and penalties of 40% for deliberate non-disclosure (manquement délibéré, Article 1729 CGI) or 80% for artificial transactions (abus de droit, Article 1729-0 bis CGI); criminal prosecution for VAT fraud under Article 1741 CGI exposes the entity and managers to a fine up to €500,000 and five years' imprisonment; customs export fraud under Article 414-1 Code des douanes carries up to three years' imprisonment, confiscation and a fine up to the value of the machinery; export proceeds not repatriated within 180 days without documented credit terms may be challenged as disguised capital export under the Code monétaire et financier, and participation in intra-EU fraud carousels triggers joint liability of the entity and its managers (Article L267 LPF).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), with prudential supervision delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) and balance-of-payments statistical governance coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the French Ministry of Economy and Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the euro area and operates no exchange-control licensing regime. The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions pursuant to EU Treaty freedoms, the EU Capital Movement Directive, and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Profit remittance by a French SARL is unrestricted: dividend distributions require a valid shareholder approval (Assemblée Générale Ordinaire), audited financial statements where statutory thresholds are met, and standard withholding tax treatment under French tax law, with no residual convertibility hurdle. Cross-border financial flows retain only statistical reporting obligations: any individual non-resident-to-resident transaction or offsetting item exceeding €750,000 must be reported by the intermediary bank or, where applicable, the SARL, to the Banque de France within the prescribed balance-of-payments survey deadlines.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender rules, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export receipts. A French SARL may freely hold, convert, or offset foreign-currency receivables from used heavy-machinery exports, whether invoiced in EUR, USD, or third-country currencies. The only compliance duty is statistical: export flows exceeding €750,000 per transaction or aggregated annual thresholds must be captured in the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting framework, in practice submitted by the SARL banking counterparty through the OF (Opérations Financières) reporting channel; exporters opening dedicated foreign-currency accounts (comptes en devises) must disclose the account relationship to the bank, which handles ongoing reporting declarations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank / LCL
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance Account (LC and guarantees)
Cross-Border Operational Account / FX Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a sole banking underpinning; Medium viability only as a non-critical ancillary account. ACPR-regulated French electronic-money institutions and payment institutions (Qonto, Shine, Mangopay) can provide euro-denominated operational accounts for day-to-day expense flows under PSD2, and EEA-licensed EMIs may passport into France under the single-licence regime. However, non-EEA offshore digital EMIs (UK post-Brexit, US, BVI, or Asian virtual-banking platforms) cannot legally offer payment services to a French SARL without a full French/EEA licence, and none can issue documentary commercial letters of credit, standby guarantees, or structured FX hedging lines. Given the medium-risk enhanced profile of used-construction-excavator remarketing and the mandatory SWIFT/LC clearing rails in the target payment architecture, a tier-1 commercial bank account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French statutory AML/KYC rules (Articles L.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code) do not prescribe an absolute physical-presence requirement, but in practice tier-1 banks mandate an in-person or hybrid-video identity verification for the SARL's gérant and any 25%+ beneficial owners. For non-resident directors and shareholders opening from outside the EEA, most French commercial banks require a physical visit to a French branch or an equivalent face-to-face interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer; identity documents must be certified, and for non-EU documents apostilled and translated by a sworn translator. A subset of French banks and licensed neobanks permit fully remote onboarding via video KYC for EEA-resident individuals and simple corporate structures, but documentary heavy-trade, LC, and FX-treasury mandates will in every case push the bank to request a supplementary in-person senior-management interview and completion of a fact-finding onboarding form for the trade cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Onboarding of a used heavy-machinery trading company flagged under Enhanced Due Diligence; bank queries the provenance and physical existence of traded excavators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent SGS/Bureau Veritas pre-shipment inspection certificates; notarized bill of sale and prior owner registration certificates; full invoice chain from original dealer/manufacturer; CMR waybills and EU import customs declarations; export-control screening statement confirming the goods are not dual-use items under Regulation (EU) 2021/821; proof of registration of the company in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership above 25%, particularly from jurisdictions outside the EEA, triggering a requirement to trace ultimate wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RBE extract from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; complete corporate chart with each intermediate holding level; certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; legalized/notarized beneficial-ownership declarations; source-of-wealth letter supported by bank statements, audited financial statements, or tax returns; personal identification numbers for the gérant and shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement risks: instructions to remit supplier proceeds to accounts in third countries or to payment intermediaries that are unrelated to the excavator seller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial purchase agreements naming the exact contractual counterparty; proforma invoices and commercial invoices; CMR or bill-of-lading evidence matching transaction value; bank letter confirming beneficiary account ownership; executed debt-assignment or payment-mandate deed (acte de cession de créance) when a broker or remarketing agent acts as settlement conduit; anti-money-laundering declaration on the origin and destination of funds for each unusual payment instruction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons or reputational-concentration risk in public-financed construction projects where secondhand machinery could be linked to state procurement or conflict zones.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-KYC PEP self-declaration for shareholders, gérant, and beneficial owners; comprehensive item-level provenance register (machine serial number, previous plates/registrations, auction house records, decommissioning certificates); commitment letter to Enhanced Monitoring with automated transaction surveillance; end-user undertaking prohibiting re-export to sanctioned jurisdictions; OECD/SANTA due diligence declarations for brokers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-volume mismatch: expected SWIFT traffic in EUR/USD/JPY for large-ticket excavators inconsistent with modest stated share capital or short operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder board resolution authorizing the treasury and FX framework; forward-looking cash-flow forecasts bridging purchase and resale cycles; audited financial statements for prior years where available; trade-receivables ageing ledger; evidence of shareholder subordinated loans (comptes courants d'associés) with notarial declaration of funds; documented economic rationale for each machinery transaction in the deal pipeline.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital inflows are liberalized: an EU or third-country shareholder may inject funds into the SARL as either equity (augmentation de capital) or shareholder loan (apport en compte courant d'associé) without Banque de France authorization. The compliant routing protocol is a SWIFT MT103 wire to the SARL's euro-denominated IBAN at its tier-1 French bank, referencing the purpose code covering 'equity injection for working capital' (EC01/EC02 category mapping) or, for loans, the transaction-type code for 'loans to affiliated enterprises.' For clarity in bank compliance review, the originator's payment message must identify the ultimate originator and the underlying capital-deed date. For share capital increases exceeding a minimal threshold, the SARL files the M-form (Acte de constitution de garantie/modification) with the Guichet Unique and the Greffe; cash injections above €10,000 sourced from cash require a fund-origin declaration. Cross-border capital contributions above €750,000 are captured automatically in the bank's balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France; the bank issues a traçabilité record for audit. If funds arrive in a convertible currency (USD, JPY), the receiving bank executes the conversion on a spot deal and books the euro proceeds; no FX license is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement relies on three rails: (1) SEPA Instant/SCT for euro payments to EEA suppliers and intra-EU trade, cleared via TARGET2; (2) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for extra-EEA payments (Japan, Korea, Gulf states, Africa) with all commercial terms governed by the underlying sales contract; and (3) documentary commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) issued under ICC UCP 600 by the French bank in favor of the machinery supplier, secured by the import contract, proforma invoice, and shipping documents (bill of lading/CMR, inspection certificate, insurance policy). Where the SARL sells to auction houses or sovereign buyers, standby letters of credit under ISP98 or upstream documentary collections under URC 522 may be used. For export-risk mitigation, Bpifrance Assurance Export guarantees and post-shipment financing can be mobilized on the dossier of the export receivable. Contractual payment splits (e.g., 30% advance via MT103, 70% against documents under LC) are standard for used excavator transactions; every MT103 must carry the SARL's bank (Originator) or beneficiary (for supplier-side) reference and the exact invoice number to avoid FATF-related wire-transmission opacity flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/JPY forward contracts (marché à terme) documented under a French bank master agreement (often the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement or ISDA 2002 with French-law governing provisions), requiring board authorization and a signed stabilization/treasury line.
FX swaps (rollover/simplified swaps) to manage short-term mismatches between USD/JPY receipt streams and EUR disbursement obligations.
Vanilla European-style currency options, including zero-premium collars and participating forwards, for asymmetric protection on large-ticket excavator trades.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY swaps) permissible solely for long-term shareholder capital or intercompany financing structures where a matched-maturity base risk exists.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the EUR/USD, EUR/JPY, or EUR/GBP pairs because those currencies are fully convertible; NDF availability is restricted to transactions against non-convertible currencies, which do not arise in this SARL's ordinary used-construction-machinery trade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of members approving the annual financial statements (assemblee generale ordinaire annuelle, Article L. 223-26 of the French Commercial Code)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL; meeting recorded in the statutory minutes register (no external filing at this step)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the close of the financial year; a 31 December year-end requires approval no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any member may petition the Commercial Court to appoint a court agent (mandataire de justice) to convene the meeting at the company's expense; prolonged failure to approve accounts constitutes mismanagement exposing the gérant to civil liability and may justify the appointment of an ad hoc administrator.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual statutory accounts and supporting documents (comptes annuels, gestion report, profit appropriation proposal) with the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce via the INPI Guichet Unique / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval of the accounts; a 31 December year-end approved on 30 June must be filed no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to EUR 6,000 under Article L. 247-1 of the French Commercial Code, plus a possible judicial coercive order (astreinte) of up to EUR 1,500 per day; failure to file for 12 consecutive months triggers RNE strike-off (radiation) and loss of standing in court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale No. 2065-SD with No. 2050 series schedules) and activity report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via mandatory electronic filing (EDI/EFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: no later than the second working day after 1 May of the following year (in practice 4 or 5 May); for other year-ends, within three months of the balance sheet date unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the assessed corporate income tax plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; non-filing opens a three-year tax reassessment window and may trigger the automatic taxation of untaxed profits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual property-based business contribution return (CFE, declaration No. 2042-E)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP via the company's professional online taxpayer account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 December for the current tax year; a nil or first-year exemption declaration must still be filed if no taxable base exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing increase of 5% plus 0.20% monthly late interest; failure to declare the taxable base may lead to automatic assessment based on the most recent known base and issuance of an enforcement notice (avis de mise en recouvrement).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final annual value-added contribution (CVAE) reconciliation and balance payment for the last chargeable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP via online filing of declaration No. 1477-CVAE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final return and balance payment due by the second working day after 1 May for the 2024 tax year; CVAE is abolished for tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2025 under the French 2025 Finance Act, so no CVAE obligation arises for 2025 and later years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; unpaid instalments may be subject to enforced collection and the loss of the EUR 500 minimum threshold exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) update and consistency confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI / Guichet Unique and the greffe of the Trade and Companies Registry; register kept at the registered office for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any alteration in the beneficial ownership structure; no standalone mandatory annual re-declaration exists in French law, but accuracy is confirmed at the annual accounts filing date on the RNE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or knowingly false statements in the beneficial ownership register trigger criminal and administrative monetary penalties under the Monetary and Financial Code, suspension of subsequent RCS/RNE filings, and possible refusal of dividend distributions until regularisation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation (declaration CA12) under the simplified VAT regime or final annual VAT position of monthly CA3 filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP via online VAT filing (impots.gouv.fr professional account)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simplified-regime companies: CA12 annual return filed by 19 April following the calendar year; actual-regime companies (turnover above EUR 840,000): monthly CA3 filings by the 25th of the following month and no separate annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the net VAT due plus 0.20% monthly interest; non-payment triggers garnishment procedures, recovery of tax from the gérant's personal assets in cases of deliberate concealment, and suspension of VAT deduction rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a French SARL when two of the three following thresholds are exceeded at the previous financial year-end: total balance sheet above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. The audit obligation also arises when the SARL controls or is controlled by other companies requiring consolidated supervision, and shareholders representing at least one-tenth of capital may petition the court to appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable General per ANC Regulation 2014-03) is mandatory for SARL statutory annual accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the European Union is permitted only for consolidated financial statements and is not available for the individual annual accounts filed with the RNE or the tax authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law imposes no separate annual UBO affirmation form; the beneficial ownership register (RBE) must be kept permanently at the registered office and any modification must be filed with the RNE within 30 days of the event. The annual accounts filing cycle serves as the practical reconciliation point at which registry staff verify consistency between the beneficial ownership declaration, the share transfer register and the latest shareholder register. Natural persons holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of share capital or voting rights, or exercising actual control, must always be identified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share transfer register (registre des mouvements de titres et cessions de parts sociales)
Minutes register of shareholders' decisions (registre des decisions de l'associe unique or minutes of general meetings)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des beneficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 325 – USD 650 per year for professional domiciliation and registered-office services in a commercial city location; EUR 200 – EUR 400 typical outside metropolitan Paris
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,600 – USD 27,000 per year for a statutory audit of a mid-size wholesale SARL (EUR 8,000 – EUR 25,000); voluntary smaller-scale audits range from USD 4,000 to USD 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate; reduced rate of 11% on first €42,500 of profit for companies with turnover < €10M)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate for small businesses (11% on first €42,500); research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) for qualifying R&D; no specific incentives for trading activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the EFI (Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) portal or the impots.gouv.fr professional space.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is 3 May of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends, deadline is within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide turnover attributable to French permanent establishment; if no PE, file only if French-source income.
Compute based on French GAAP; adjust for transfer pricing adjustments if applicable.
Apply tax adjustments (e.g., non-deductible expenses, tax credits).
Include CIR, CII, and foreign tax credits; attach supporting schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax due if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if filed after 30 days; 80% if filed after 30 days following a formal notice. Interest at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571 (Quarterly Instalment Payment) filed electronically via the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December of the current fiscal year, based on prior year's tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of instalment (1/4 of prior year's tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with French PE must pay instalments; if no prior year tax, pay estimated current year tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for tax credits or reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduce instalment by expected tax credits (e.g., CIR).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment penalty: 5% of unpaid instalment plus interest at 0.20% per month; additional 0.5% per month for repeated non-payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (reduced to 25% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if parent holds ≥10% for 2 years; further reduced under tax treaties, e.g., 0% for certain treaty partners)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit Form 5000 (Certificate of Tax Residence) to the French tax authority, along with proof of beneficial ownership and holding period. For EU parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt withholding if conditions are met; file Form 5000 and a declaration of eligibility.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33%; reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive for associated companies (≥25% holding) and under many tax treaties (e.g., 0% with US, 10% with China). Interest: statutory 30%; reduced to 0% under EU directive for associated companies; treaty rates typically 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million turnover or assets (or group threshold) for full Local File and Master File; below this, simplified documentation (Form 2257) is required for companies with turnover > €50 million or with related-party transactions exceeding €1 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies substance-over-form and anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155-A, abuse of law doctrine). Companies must demonstrate real economic activity (employees, premises, decision-making) to benefit from tax treaties and EU directives. The French tax administration may challenge shell companies lacking substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of turnover or profits, false invoicing, or concealment of assets in related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 CGI); civil penalty of 80% of evaded tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, no employees, no premises, and no decision-making in France, while claiming treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, 40% penalty for lack of substance, and potential criminal charges for abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for additional taxes and penalties; possible ban from managing companies in France.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures (KYC, transaction monitoring) for high-value machinery trades, or accepting cash payments above €1,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to €5 million or 5% of turnover (Monetary and Financial Code); criminal penalties for money laundering up to 10 years imprisonment and €750,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for AML breaches; personal fines and imprisonment; travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for used excavators or services that deviate from arm's length, without proper documentation, leading to profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with 40% penalty (or 80% if deemed abusive); interest at 0.20% per month; potential criminal charges for tax evasion if intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-arm's length transactions; possible criminal prosecution.
